sources.entry: WebThings Gateway - WebThings is an open source implementation of the Web of Things, including the WebThings Gateway and the WebThings Framework. (Source Code) MPL-2.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: WebThings Gateway is a self-hosted Node.js web app for monitoring and controlling a building over the web, acting as an open source Web of Things gateway.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes WebThings Gateway as a self-hosted web application for monitoring and controlling a building over the web, and as an open source Web of Things gateway. It is recommended to install via Docker image as of the 2.0 release, with an experimental snap package and build-from-source options also mentioned. The source build uses npm and nvm for Node.js, with native dependencies for Bluetooth, DBus, USB and Python 3 add-ons on Ubuntu/Debian, Fedora and macOS. The HTTPS server can use a Let's Encrypt-based or a self-signed SSL certificate, or a provided tunneling service to set up a webthings.io domain. The source layout mentions add-on management for Zigbee and Z-Wave, a rules engine, an SQLite3 database, push notifications, and Handlebars views. The README does not describe the Docker or snap setup in detail.
use_cases: monitor and control a building over the web
run a self-hosted Web of Things gateway
manage IoT devices through add-ons such as Zigbee and Z-Wave
create rules to automate connected devices
access a home gateway remotely with a tunnel domain
how_to_run: Recommended: install using the Docker image (see project documentation)
Build from source: git clone the repository and cd into gateway
nvm install && nvm use (uses .nvmrc for Node version)
Open the web interface in a browser and follow setup instructions
notable: Open source implementation of the Web of Things standard
Add-on system for protocols such as Zigbee and Z-Wave
Optional tunneling service for a webthings.io domain
Supports custom SSL certificates or self-signed certificates
caveats: Bluetooth access on Linux requires setcap permissions on node and python3 binaries
Browser tests need Google Chrome and a JDK
Self-signed certificate setups require a browser security exception
Snap package is described as experimental
